anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

pass_a_gloss: And so that we may understand more clearly we shall take another thing: if more woods should lie near one another, upon all we shall find the beginning — for each wood even to the last has its own beginning — but one only, the first lying, has the first. And the first, being first according to placing, has also its own beginning, but the next, having fallen out of the first, each has its own beginning.
pass_b_english: And so that we may understand [more clearly], we shall take [another] thing. If several logs should lie near one another, we shall find the beginning in all of them — for each log, even to the last, has its own beginning — but only the one lying first has the first. And the first, being first according to position, has also its own beginning. Those that follow, having fallen out of the first, each have their own beginning.
source_text: Καὶ [ἵν]α σαφ[έστερον σ]υνῶμε[ν], [ἕτ]ερόν [τι λη]ψ[ό]μεθα· εἰ ξύλα [πλεί]ονα κέοιτο πλησίον ἀλ[λήλω]ν, ἐπὶ μὲν πάντων τὴ[ν] ἀρχὴν εὑρήσομεν – ἔχει γὰρ ἕκαστον ξύλον μέχρι καὶ τοῦ τελευταίου ἀρχὴν ἰδίαν –, ἓν δὲ μόνον τὸ πρῶτον κείμενον ἔχει τὸ πρῶτον. Καὶ τὸ μὲν πρῶτον κατὰ τὴν θέσιν πρῶτον ὂν ἔχει|| καὶ τὴν ἰδίαν ἀρχήν, τὰ δὲ ἑξῆς ἐκπεσόντα τοῦ πρώτου ἔχει ἕκαστον ἀρχὴν τὴν αὐτοῦ.
